name: Conditional lower bounds for subset sum: SETH, k-SUM and lattice-hardness reductions
description: Survey-style item on what fine-grained complexity says about subset sum. ABHS (arXiv 1704.04546) prove that Bellman's O*(t) cannot be improved to t^{1-eps} 2^{o(n)} under SETH; Bringmann-Wellnitz (arXiv 2010.09096) extend this to a dense-regime dichotomy under SETH plus Strong k-SUM; the k-SUM conjecture says n^{ceil(k/2)} is essentially optimal. Jin-Williams-Zhang (ESA 2025) give O*(2^{n/3}) for Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum (PESS); the task outline ties PESS to lattice hardness. No known conditional result rules in or out a 2^{(1/2-eps)n} worst-case algorithm for {0,1} subset sum, so C1/C2 are neither implied nor contradicted by any listed hypothesis.
authors_year_venue: Abboud-Bringmann-Hermelin-Shabtay, ACM TALG 2022, arXiv 1704.04546; Bringmann-Wellnitz SODA 2021, arXiv 2010.09096; Jin-Williams-Zhang ESA 2025 (LIPIcs 351, 86:1-86:12); Jin-Wu ICALP 2024 (LIPIcs 297, 94); Lampis 'k-SUM hardness implies treewidth-SETH' SODA 2026 (cited in 2608.07309); Chukhin-Kulikov-Levitskii-Mihajlin arXiv 2608.07309 (context on k-SUM).
status_and_verification: Peer-reviewed venues for ABHS, BW, JWZ and Jin-Wu. I read only abstracts via web search for ABHS, BW and JWZ, plus statements about them in the full text of 2601.01390 and 2608.07309. I did not read the lattice-hardness content of JWZ; the lattice link is taken from the task outline and a search snippet, so it is unverified.
key_theorem_or_bound: ABHS: Subset Sum has no O(T^{1-eps} 2^{o(n)})-time algorithm unless SETH fails (T = target). BW: if Subset Sum is near-linear time for any setting with t << max_X * Sigma_X / n^2 then SETH and Strong k-SUM both fail; matching algorithm for t >> max_X Sigma_X / n^2. k-SUM conjecture: no O(n^{ceil(k/2) - eps}). JWZ: PESS in O*(2^{n/3}) (improving Jin-Wu 2^{0.4n} and the 2^{n/2} of Allcock et al.); Chukhin et al. quantum: Pigeonhole Modular ESS in O*(3^{2n/7}) = 2^{0.453n}.
regime_exponents: SETH/k-SUM results live in the pseudopolynomial window t = 2^{Theta(n)} down to poly(n), with exponent tight in t, and say nothing about the exponent 1/2 of the exponential-time MITM bound: best worst-case is 2^{n/2}/n^{0.5023} (Chen-Jin-Randolph-Servedio 2023, quoted in 2608.07309). Relevant constants for C1/C2: 0.5n baseline, AKKN 0.661n, PESS n/3 ~ 0.333n; the C2 threshold 0.311n sits just below the PESS 1/3 exponent, which is suggestive but not a proven connection.
proof_type_and_tools: Fine-grained reductions: k-SAT to dense Subset Sum (ABHS, via number-encoded clause satisfaction), reductions from k-SUM and SETH (BW), and for PESS an algorithmic rather than reduction-based argument (Jin-Williams-Zhang use refinements of Jin-Wu's representation-style technique); lattice connection: [uncertain] not verified.
quantitative_loss: SETH reductions are tight up to 2^{o(n)} and polylogarithmic factors in t, so they do not survive being converted into constant-in-the-exponent statements such as 2^{0.311n}; any proof of C1/C2 giving an O*(2^{(1/2-eps)n}) algorithm would not contradict SETH-based bounds because those concern T^{1-eps} with T up to 2^{Theta(n)} (target size), not the 2^{n/2} bound. Reduction overheads (poly(n) blowups) are polynomial and unproblematic.
worst_case_vs_average_case: All hypotheses are worst-case. The lattice/average-case hardness tie (Lagarias-Odlyzko, SIS-style hardness) is average-case/cryptographic and does not transfer to a worst-case statement; low-density average-case subset sum is easy by lattice reduction, which is why dense random instances are the hard ones.
coefficient_set: {0,1} Subset Sum (ABHS, BW); PESS is the {-1,0,1} (two disjoint equal-sum subsets) variant, so the result concerns the coefficient set {-1,0,1}, which is exactly the relation set used by C1/C2's equal-sum pairs.
subset_size_regime: k-SUM has fixed k; SETH-hardness for Subset Sum uses all subsets. PESS output subsets are unconstrained size. C1/C2 want Theta(n)-subsets, which fall outside these hardness statements.
relevance_to_Nc: A proof of C1 (N_c small or the input in a large-bin regime) would imply a 2^{(1/2-eps)n} algorithm for {0,1} subset sum (via AKKN-style combination), which would refute the (unproved) hypothesis that MITM is optimal but contradict no SETH-based lower bound; it would however imply a faster-than-2^{n/2} algorithm for a problem on which the k-SUM-based intuition (n^{ceil(k/2)} optimal, with k = n/b blocks) predicts no improvement, so a proof would be a notable non-trivial consequence. Conversely, a counterexample family with huge N_c and intermediate bins would be consistent with conditional hardness. PESS-type guarantee (pigeonhole forces equal-sum disjoint pairs when sum < 2^n) is the unconditional version of N_c >= 1.
relevance_to_Dstar: C2 says hard instances cannot have few distinct balanced half-sums; refuting C2 would produce hard instances with D* <= 2^{0.311n} (structured), while proving C2 would imply every instance with D* <= 2^{0.311n} is solvable faster than 2^{n/2}. The PESS exponent 1/3 and k-SUM block structure suggest comparing D* to 2^{n/3}, but no theorem makes this link. [uncertain] speculative, not derived in a source.
applicability_gap: SETH and k-SUM lower bounds are about t^{1-eps} or fixed-k n^{k/2} scaling, not about the 2^{n/2} MITM exponent; hence they neither support nor refute C1/C2. Lattice hardness is average-case and for low density. No known reduction from SETH or k-SUM to a 2^{(1/2-eps)n} lower bound for {0,1} subset sum. Chukhin et al. show the k-SUM conjecture is implied/related to treewidth-SETH (Lampis), but still far from the exponential regime.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Hard families: ABHS SAT-encoding instances (dense, t ~ 2^{n}/poly), random numbers with density ~1 (lattice-hard region, Lagarias-Odlyzko fails near density 1), dissociated/Sidon-like sets for D* and N_c extremes. Instances satisfying pigeonhole (sum < 2^n) always contain equal-sum pairs (N_c >= 1 for PESS).
dependency_chain: Chain: SETH/k-SUM (ABHS, BW) bounds the pseudopolynomial end; AKKN density dichotomy handles the bin-size parameter; Randolph-Wegrzycki representation technique and JWZ PESS algorithm handle the {-1,0,1} relation view; C1/C2 sit in the intermediate band. Chan 2601.01390 explicitly quotes ABHS as the matching lower bound to his deterministic O~(t).
constructiveness: Hardness reductions are constructive (explicit instance maps), but do not yield algorithms. PESS algorithms (JWZ) are constructive randomized O*(2^{n/3}).
lean_formalizable: Reductions are not realistic to formalize here. The only elementary formalizable fact is the pigeonhole existence of two distinct equal-sum subsets when the total is < 2^n - 1 (PESS), already relevant as N_c >= 1.
computational_check: Not applicable at n<=40 for SETH statements. For PESS, the repo scripts could enumerate all subsets for n<=30 and count equal-sum disjoint pairs, giving empirical N_c for pigeonhole-regime inputs; no source reports such counts.
next_experiment: Write down precisely which consequences a proof of C1 would have in the 'subset sum is hard' map: (i) a 2^{(1/2-eps)n} {0,1} algorithm, (ii) check it does not contradict ABHS parameters by placing the hard ABHS instances (t ~ 2^{n}/poly(n) dense) inside the large-bin branch of C1 (they have bin size ~2^{n}/poly, i.e. beta > 2^{0.661n}), which would be a consistency check on C1.
open_issues: Lattice-hardness tie of JWZ not verified. Whether 2^{(1/2-eps)n} for {0,1} subset sum contradicts any standard hypothesis is open (no known lower bound beyond k-SUM heuristics). [uncertain] claim that ABHS instances lie in the large-bin regime is my inference.
